subject.title: fix(commands): re-check owner for cross-channel /allowlist writes

question: Should origin channel/account and context-derived ownership remain scope-local for cross-scope `/allowlist` writes, with explicit `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, its configured wildcard, and trusted internal `operator.admin` as the global-authority paths?
rationale: The patch closes a concrete persistent privilege escalation but deliberately denies an existing implicit cross-scope workflow, so the permanent security and upgrade contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Adopt scoped authority
options.body: Approve target-scope reauthorization and direct operators needing cross-scope administration to configure `commands.ownerAllowFrom` explicitly.

options.title: Require explicit identities only
options.body: Also remove configured wildcard authority for cross-scope writes and require a named owner identity or trusted gateway admin.

options.title: Preserve implicit cross-scope access
options.body: Keep origin-only owners able to administer unrelated scopes and accept the reported privilege boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped authority
recommendation.body: Approve target-scope reauthorization and direct operators needing cross-scope administration to configure `commands.ownerAllowFrom` explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across both the authorization resolver and allowlist/config-write path.
